A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Semantic ODE study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched despite appendix reflow and table renumbering.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B report original benchmark results, pharmacokinetic case studies, SIR simulations, bifurcation experiments, and evaluations on real datasets.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B retain these original empirical investigations, with revised numerical results and some updated fitted-model visualizations.

M1.justification: The composition/property-map training and trajectory predictors remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 corrects a loop-index typo from b to i, and Figure 6 explicitly evaluates predictions at observation times, as Algorithm 2 already did. These clarify the existing procedure rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The five synthetic benchmark problems, Duffing oscillator, real tumor-growth and drug-concentration datasets, SIR example, bifurcation experiment, and temporal and initial-condition extrapolation scenarios remain. Removing the duplicated appendix benchmark table does not remove coverage.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain SINDy, SINDy-5, WSINDy, WSINDy-5, PySR-20, Neural ODE, Neural Laplace, and DeepONet. The pharmacokinetic sparsity comparisons and Semantic ODE* variant also remain. The removed black-box comparison subsection duplicated comparisons already in Table 3.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 changes the stated data supplied to Semantic ODE from combined test and validation sets to combined train and validation sets, substantially revising the reported separation between fitting and testing. E.2 also revises the logistic-growth composition limit from three to two motifs. The PDFs do not establish whether these corrections reflect rerun experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 10 revises the diagnostic evidence showing how candidate compositions fit individual pharmacokinetic trajectories. Figures 7, 8, and 13 also update the fitted, edited, and extrapolated property-map case studies. These refresh existing analyses without introducing new ablation or robustness questions.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark averages and standard deviations across five random seeds and data splits. The bifurcation plot retains its uncertainty display. Revised means and standard-deviation values do not change the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and the Duffing table (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 6) revise numerical results. Semantic ODE's pharmacokinetic RMSEs become 0.015/0.197 instead of 0.023/0.211 for low/high noise, replacing SINDy/Neural ODE as the respective reported leaders. Duffing RMSEs change from 0.090/0.251 to 0.096/0.236. Plotted fits and losses also change. The revised protocol descriptions prevent assuming same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–3, Lemmas 1–2, motif definitions, and spline and asymptotic derivations are retained. The removed theorem passage duplicates retained Theorem 1, and the rewritten proof opening restates the same argument. Remaining mathematical edits correct notation rather than change substantive reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim direct semantic modeling enables understandable, editable, flexible dynamical models without post-hoc equation analysis. Although v2 removes the abstract's concluding experiment-summary sentence, the introduction and discussion retain the same scientific contributions and scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of comprehensibility, editing, noise robustness, and generalization remain. Section 7 and Appendix G retain the limitations concerning finite compositions, oscillatory and chaotic extrapolation, dimensionality, motif parameterization, and interventions. Updated results introduce no substantive new explanation or qualification.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 fills a substantial reproducibility gap by documenting all three neural baselines: standardization, network choices, Adam training for 200 epochs, batch sizes, Optuna, and hyperparameter ranges in new Tables 13–15. These are newly disclosed settings, not established changes to those experiments. V2 also adds a laboratory code-repository address.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Optuna and Adam, plus Kacprzyk and van der Schaar's 2025 work on task-specific symbolic-regression complexity. Appendix F adds a corresponding observation about the difficulty of designing constraints for analyzable equations. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the abstract, makes scattered grammatical and terminology corrections, removes a redundant appendix comparison subsection and theorem restatement, and adds localized implementation descriptions. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 removes duplicated v1 Table 6 and adds hyperparameter Tables 13–15. Figure 6 is corrected, Figures 7, 8, 10, and 13 are redrawn with updated plotted content and some legend adjustments, and Table 3 loses its shaded Semantic ODE row. Appendix floats are repositioned without a broad layout redesign.

improvement.justification: The added neural-baseline specifications and corrected split description improve reproducibility and internal consistency. Removing duplicate material and correcting pseudocode also help clarity. These are limited net gains: the relationship between revised scores and setting corrections remains unexplained, and the new Neural Laplace paragraph is mislabeled DeepONet. Scientific coverage, core contributions, and theoretical support remain essentially unchanged.
